payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

outcomes.description: Add a helmet to the woman.
outcomes.target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.
outcomes.reference: The woman in the input image.

nodes.question: Does the image show a helmet visibly on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a helmet is visibly on the woman’s head; fail if the image clearly shows no helmet on her head; unknown if the woman or her head is not visible enough to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess only the woman in the input image and whether she is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head. Ignore unrelated edits.

nodes.question: Is there image evidence that a helmet has been added to the woman, even if the requested result is not complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows a helmet on or being placed on the woman’s head, but the evidence does not establish the complete result in s1; fail if the image clearly shows no progress toward adding a helmet; unknown if visibility is insufficient to determine whether such progress occurred. A complete result is not partial progress.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible evidence of progress toward giving the woman in the input image a helmet. Do not count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Is a helmet visibly present on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 passes. Partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. Absent if s1 and s2 both fail. Unknown if neither complete nor partial nor absent is established because a required check is unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; unknown evidence remains unresolved.
nodes.binding: Target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.. Reference: The woman in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node already matches the instruction and evidence: the edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and the complete check passes with high confidence and full aggregate agreement. No semantic change is indicated. Preserve the distinction between complete fulfillment and progress-only evidence, and retain the unknown path for genuinely insufficient visual evidence; do not infer extra requirements from the source image or the reference label.
s2: No semantic change is indicated: the edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and the node correctly treats this as progress while leaving complete fulfillment to the parent check. Preserve the distinction between progress and completion, and retain the unknown path for genuinely insufficient visual evidence. The high-confidence pass and full aggregate agreement provide no basis for changing the binding or criteria.
s1: No semantic change is indicated. The edited image visibly shows a helmet on the woman’s head, and the node passes with high confidence and full aggregate agreement. Preserve the current subject-specific criterion and the unknown path for genuinely insufficient visual evidence; do not infer extra requirements from the source image or reference label.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout cannot faithfully distinguish a complete result from partial progress. s2 is defined to pass only when it shows progress but does not establish the complete result in s1, yet the readout says partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. If s1 is unknown while s2 passes, this can label the result partial without establishing incompleteness; if s1 fails, the checks may also conflict about whether a helmet is present. The composition should require evidenced incompleteness before assigning partial and resolve contradictory support observations rather than treating them as a valid outcome.

transaction.reason: The existing checks and traces support complete fulfillment, but the rejection identifies a genuine ambiguity in the readout when complete evidence is unknown or support observations conflict. Add a nested check that independently verifies whether the visible helmet is actually on the woman’s head, using the existing progress observation as context, then require explicit evidence of incompleteness before assigning partial.

actions.question: Independently, does the edited image visibly show a helmet on the head of the woman from the source image, and is that evidence clear enough to establish the requested result?
actions.criteria: Pass if a helmet is clearly visible on the source-image woman’s head; fail if her head is sufficiently visible and clearly has no helmet; unknown if identity, visibility, or helmet placement cannot be determined.
actions.binding: Inspect only the edited image and the woman identified in the source image. Determine whether a helmet is visibly on her head; do not infer from unrelated edits or from the source image’s lack of a helmet.

actions.criteria: For R1, complete only when s1 and s3 both pass. Partial only when s1 and s3 both fail and s2 passes, establishing progress while also establishing incompleteness. Absent only when s1, s3, and s2 all fail. If s1 and s3 disagree, either is unknown, or the required evidence otherwise does not establish one of these states, return unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not preserve the requested property consistently. s1 asks whether a helmet is on the woman in the input image, while s3 asks about the edited image and identifies her by comparison with the source. The fulfillment rule requires both to pass, so it can reject a correctly edited image merely because the source woman did not already wear a helmet. Also, s2’s progress criterion is defined relative to s1’s result, although s1 assesses the source image rather than the edited result; this makes partial/absent composition unsound. The readout therefore cannot reliably distinguish completion, progress, and no progress.

transaction.reason: The existing traces establish the requested helmet, but the rejected repair exposed a real composition issue: progress must be assessed independently of the complete-result check, and partial requires evidence of both progress and incompleteness. Add a nested, independent check of the edited image’s helmet placement, then make the readout conservative when observations conflict or are unknown.

actions.question: In the edited image, is a helmet visibly on the head of the woman from the source image?
actions.criteria: Pass if a helmet is clearly visible on the source-image woman’s head in the edited image; fail if her head is sufficiently visible and clearly has no helmet; unknown if her identity, head visibility, or helmet placement cannot be determined.
actions.binding: Assess the edited image, using the source image only to identify the woman. Judge visible helmet placement on her head; do not require that she wore a helmet in the source image, and ignore unrelated edits.

actions.question: Does the edited image show visible progress toward giving the source-image woman a helmet, whether or not the requested result is complete?
actions.criteria: Pass if the edited image visibly shows a helmet on or being placed on the source-image woman’s head; fail if the relevant head is sufficiently visible and there is no such helmet or placement; unknown if visibility or identity is insufficient. This check assesses progress, not completeness.
actions.binding: Assess visible evidence in the edited image, using the source image only to identify the woman. Do not count unrelated changes as progress.

actions.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 passes. Partial only if s1 fails and s2 passes, establishing visible progress while the complete-result check establishes incompleteness. Absent only if s1 and s2 both fail. If s1 is unknown, or the observations otherwise conflict or fail to establish one of these states, return unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide independent, coherent evidence for the requested outcome. s1 and s3 both test essentially the same complete-result condition, while s2 is activated under s3 but has no dependency on it and defines progress as incomplete relative to s1. The fulfillment rule then requires both s1 and s3 to fail before it can recognize partial progress, even though s1 failing means the woman’s head is clearly visible without a helmet and does not establish that a helmet is being added. This can reject valid partial progress and leaves the composition dependent on redundant, potentially conflicting checks. The program should use evidence that distinguishes completion, progress, and no progress without treating a coarse or duplicate check as proof of a finer condition.

The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence for the rubric’s progress and completion distinction. s1 asks about the source image, so it cannot establish whether the edit completed the request; s3 checks the edited image, but s2’s progress criterion is internally inconsistent: it requires evidence that the result is not complete in s1, even though s1 is a source-image observation. The fulfillment rule then requires both s1 and s3 to fail before it can count s2 as partial, which can reject genuine partial progress and does not faithfully compose the available evidence. The nested activation and dependencies also make s2’s evidence depend on s3 while its criterion refers to s1. Reject for unsupported and contradictory composition.

The support tree is structurally invalid: s1 asks about the source image, but its criteria and binding do not specify that image clearly, while s3 and s2 assess the edited image. More importantly, fulfillment is nested under s2, so it is activated only when s2 passes; it cannot report absent when s2 fails, despite its criteria requiring that case. The composition also requires both source and edited images to show the helmet for completion, although the request is to add one and the source need not already contain it. These defects prevent faithful completion and no-progress judgments.
